paper.title: A Nearly Instance Optimal Algorithm for Top-k Ranking under the Multinomial Logit Model

settings.name_in_paper: Active top-k ranking from multi-wise comparisons under the MNL model
unmapped: Each query is a subset S_t with 2 <= |S_t| <= l_size; the feedback is the most preferred item drawn from the multinomial logit (Plackett-Luce) choice model Pr[a|S] = theta_a / sum_{j in S} theta_j
Goal: identify the top-k items (k_top known to the learner) w.h.p.; the learner knows n, k and l
Items are labeled by a uniformly random permutation
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t$ from $1$ to $T$, the algorithm chooses a subset of items with at least two items, denoted by $S_t \subseteq \{ 1,...,n\}$, for query/comparison. The size of the set $S_t$ is upper bounded by a pre-fixed parameter $l$, i.e., $2 \leq |S_t| \leq l$. Given the set $S_t$, the agent will report her most preferred item $a \in S_t$ following the multinomial logit (MNL) model: \Pr[a |S_t] = \frac{\exp(\mu_a)}{\sum_{j\in S_t} \exp(\mu_j)}.

settings.name_in_paper: Active top-k ranking from pairwise comparisons (Bradley-Terry / MNL with l = 2)
unmapped: Bradley-Terry pairwise comparisons Pr[i beats j] = theta_i/(theta_i+theta_j); learner knows k (number of top items)
settings.definition_quote: For $l = O(\log n)$, we can always use pairwise comparisons by losing a polylog factor. Therefore, we only focus on the case when $l = 2$ in this section.

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: We design an active ranking algorithm which uses \tilde{O}(\frac{n}{l} + k + \frac{\sum_{i \geq k+1} \theta_{i}}{\theta_k} + \sum_{i \geq k + 1, \theta_i \geq \frac{\theta_k}{2}} \frac{\theta_{k}^2}{(\theta_k - \theta_i)^2} +\sum_{ i: i\leq k, \theta_i \leq 2\theta_{k+1}} \frac{\theta_{k+1}^2}{(\theta_{ k + 1} - \theta_i)^2}) comparisons with the set size at most l ... to identify the top-k items with high probability.

results.notes: O_tilde hides polylog factors of n and 1/(theta_k - theta_{k+1}). n mapped to K. High probability = 1 - 1/n^c. Number of queries via doubling of Q.

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: For any (possibly active) ranking algorithm $A$, suppose that $A$ uses comparisons of set size at most $l$. Even when the algorithm $A$ is given the values of $\{\theta_1,...,\theta_n\}$ ..., $A$ still needs \Omega(...) comparisons to identify the top-$k$ items with probability at least $7/8$.

results.notes: Restated as Corollary 3.6, obtained by combining Theorems 3.1-3.5.

source.label: thm:ublogl
source.quote: For every $m$ items with $\theta_1 \geq \theta_2 \geq \cdots \geq \theta_n$, Algorithm \ref{alg:malg_3}, on given a random permutation of labels $\Omega=[n]$ and $k$, returns top-$k$ items w.h.p. using $$ O \left(\kappa^7 \cdot \left( k + \sum_{i = k + 1}^n \frac{\theta_{k }^2}{(\theta_k - \theta_i)^2} +\sum_{i = 1}^k \frac{\theta_{k + 1 }^2}{(\theta_{ k + 1} - \theta_i)^2} \right)\right) $$ total number of pairwise comparisons.

results.notes: w.h.p. means probability 1 - 1/n^c. Pairwise comparisons only.

symbols.H_low: sum over i>=k+1 with theta_i >= theta_k/2 of theta_k^2/(theta_k-theta_i)^2

conditions: any (possibly adaptive) algorithm, comparisons of any size
with this many comparisons success probability is at most 7/8

source.label: thm:lb2ctk
source.quote: Assume $\theta_k > \theta_{k+1}$ and $c < 10^{-4}$. For any algorithm $A$ (can be adaptive), if $A$ uses $c \sum_{ i:k+1\leq i, \theta_i \geq \theta_k/2} \frac{\theta_k^2}{(\theta_k- \theta_i)^2}$ comparisons of any size ..., then $A$ will identify the top-$k$ items with probability at most $7/8$.

results.notes: Recorded as: c*H_low comparisons are insufficient for success probability > 7/8, for any c < 1e-4.
